blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An engineer reads cuOpt's log for a 900-binary capital plan solved with its defaults. Which work does the log place on the GPU?

options.text: One feasibility-jump worker, and PDLP in the root LP's race
options.says: Right: 1 GPUFJ worker beside 15 CPU ones, and PDLP racing dual simplex and barrier for the root LP.

options.text: The branch-and-bound tree, with one node on each GPU core
options.says: Cuts and branch and bound run on the CPU; the CPU works on the dual bound.

options.text: Presolve and the cutting planes, done before the root LP
options.says: Presolve ran on 4 CPU threads, and cuts run on the CPU too.

options.text: Every heuristic, while the CPU only reads in the model
options.says: 15 of the 16 feasibility-jump workers ran on the CPU, as do the other heuristics.

origin.section: cuOpt's Log Says Which Parts Run on the GPU

questions.stem: A vendor promises to move branch and bound itself onto a GPU's thousands of cores. What about the work at each node makes that hard?

options.text: Each node's LP is too large to fit in the card's memory
options.says: A node's LP is small: it differs from its parent's by one bound and is re-solved in a few pivots.

options.text: Each node's bound comes from PDLP, which is too inexact
options.says: A node's LP is re-solved from the parent's basis with dual simplex, not by PDLP.

options.text: Each node is a few small pivots, each waiting for the last
options.says: Right: small sequential steps leave thousands of cores with nothing to do on one pivot.

options.text: Each node starts from scratch, with no basis from its parent
options.says: A node's LP is re-solved from its parent's basis with dual simplex, a few pivots each.

origin.section: Branch and Bound Is a Tree of Small, Dependent Steps

questions.stem: Tonight's cuOpt run returns a capital plan with status FeasibleFound and a reported gap of 9.5e-4, against a target of 1e-3. What should the job do before handing it to HiGHS as a start?

options.text: Discard it, since only an Optimal status makes a plan usable
options.says: Both of the lesson's FeasibleFound plans passed every check; accepting only Optimal would throw them away.

options.text: Accept it as it is, since its reported gap is under the target
options.says: The check decides from the plan's own numbers, not from what the solver reported about itself.

options.text: Rerun cuOpt until two runs return the same plan, then use it
options.says: cuOpt's plans differ from run to run; the course never treats one as reproducible.

options.text: Check its rows, integrality and worth against the tightest bound
options.says: Right: feasible, integral, and within the gap of the smallest bound any solver proved.

origin.section: A cuOpt Plan Is Checked, Not Trusted
